objectives: Map request/response, event-driven, batch, and data-virtualization styles to official Integration Patterns names.
Choose synchronous request/response only when the caller must wait; otherwise event-driven or batch.
Explain that data virtualization reads remote data live without a Salesforce copy to reconcile.
Keep INT-002 API families as implementations of these styles, not replacements for them.
diagnostic_question: A user clicks Get Credit Score and must see the result; inventory changes should fan out to three systems; item master is 400k rows nightly; warehouse bins must appear live without a Salesforce table. Which of the four styles for each?
definition: Four integration styles sit on the official Salesforce Integration Patterns catalog. Request/response is Remote Process Invocation—Request and Reply: the caller waits and tracks state from the response. Event-driven work matches Fire and Forget and later event-bus tools: acknowledge and continue. Batch Data Synchronization refreshes copies in a batch manner. Data Virtualization accesses external data in real time without persisting a copy to reconcile. ([Integration Patterns](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/integration-patterns); [Data Virtualization](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/data-virtualization.html))
why_it_matters: Mixing styles—waiting on a batch, copying data you meant to virtualize, or firing events when the UI needs a score—creates timeouts, stale reports, and duplicate sources of truth.
sixty_second_explanation: Picture a restaurant pass. Request/response is the waiter standing at the pass until the plate comes back. Event-driven is the ticket spike: kitchen cooks, waiter is free, a bell rings later. Batch is tonight's inventory count after close. Data virtualization is looking through the walk-in window at the supplier's shelf instead of stocking a second fridge you must count twice.
deeper_explanation: Official timing: synchronous request/response blocks; asynchronous is nonblocking, queue, or message-based. Process + sync + Salesforce-initiated maps to Request and Reply. Process + async maps to Fire and Forget. Large copies map to Batch Data Synchronization. Live remote access without a copy is Data Virtualization / virtual integration. ([Pattern Selection Guide](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/integration-patterns))

Event-driven on the Platform is often implemented with platform events, Change Data Capture, or Pub/Sub API (INT-007). This lesson owns the style: the publisher does not wait for every consumer to finish. Request/response implementations are often REST, SOAP, Composite, or Apex callouts (INT-002/INT-006).
Batch is about how much and how fast (INT-001): thousands to millions, hours not seconds. Official Bulk intro (INT-002) is a common vehicle, not the pattern name.
Salesforce Connect powers data virtualization with external objects: a schema projection, not stored rows. INT-009 owns adapters; here you only decide whether a copy is allowed.

mental_model.analogy: A restaurant pass window: waiter waits (request/response), ticket spike (event-driven), after-hours inventory (batch), supplier fridge window (data virtualization).
useful_mapping: request/response → waiter blocks until the plate returns
event-driven → spike the ticket and keep serving
data virtualization → look at the supplier shelf; do not stock a second fridge
API family → cookware, chosen after the pass style
stored sObject copy → food in YOUR fridge (must be counted)
external object → window, not a fridge
where_it_breaks: Remote downtime is not a pretty window—users see errors unless you design fallback.
Event-driven still needs monitoring and replay (INT-007/INT-008).
Batch copies still need keys and reconciliation (INT-010).
Governors and Connect licenses are not kitchen folklore to invent.

claims.claim: Request and Reply: Salesforce invokes a remote process, waits for completion, and tracks state from the response.
Fire and Forget: Salesforce invokes a remote process but does not wait for completion; the remote side acknowledges and Salesforce continues.
Batch Data Synchronization refreshes data in Salesforce and/or an external system in a batch manner in either direction.

Data Virtualization: Salesforce accesses external data in real time, removing the need to persist and then reconcile that data. Salesforce Connect external objects are a schema projection and hold no stored rows.
claims.validation: Pattern list plus Data Virtualization architect page.

changed_in_release: Pattern names are stable; Connect adapter limits changed in recent releases—reverify INT-009, not this style lesson.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Four styles: request/response waits; event-driven acknowledges and continues; batch copies on a schedule; data virtualization reads live without a Salesforce copy. They map to official Request and Reply, Fire and Forget, Batch Data Synchronization, and Data Virtualization.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start with whether the caller must wait. If yes and volume is small, request/response. If the user must not wait, event-driven. If how much is huge, batch. If we refuse a second store, virtualize. APIs from INT-002 implement the style; they are not the style. A five-minute copy is still a copy, not virtualization.

terminology.plain: Call, wait, use the answer in this conversation.
terminology.precise: Synchronous Remote Process Invocation—Request and Reply: wait for remote completion and track state from the response.
terminology.example: Screen Get Credit Score callout that writes Score__c before the page returns.
terminology.non_example: Publishing a platform event and navigating away.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Composite API: a vehicle for request/response, not a fourth style.
terminology.boundary: INT-006 shows named-credential callouts implementing this style.

terminology.plain: Announce that something happened; do not wait for every listener to finish.
terminology.precise: Matches Fire and Forget: acknowledge and continue. Platform events/CDC/Pub/Sub (INT-007) are common implementations.
terminology.example: Opportunity Closed Won publishes an event; billing and warehouse subscribe separately.
terminology.non_example: Http.send in a Visualforce controller waiting for ERP.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Batch: scheduled bulk copy, not a per-event message (though CDC can feed batch).

terminology.plain: Move or refresh lots of rows on a schedule, not in a user click.
terminology.precise: Batch Data Synchronization: copies created or refreshed in a batch manner in either direction.
terminology.non_example: Per-save REST to ERP for each of 400,000 items.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex Batch Apex: a job type that may implement batch integration, not the pattern name itself.
terminology.boundary: Bulk vs SOAP choice is INT-002.

terminology.plain: See remote rows live; do not keep a second Salesforce table to reconcile.
terminology.precise: Official Data Virtualization: real-time access without persisting data that then needs reconciliation. Connect external objects hold no stored data.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Remote Call-In that upserts a real Account: that is a stored copy.

terminology.plain: The caller is blocked until this operation returns.
terminology.precise: Official Timing: blocking real-time request/response; result returns to the caller immediately via that operation.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: User-perceived 'real time' that is actually a later event write-back.

terminology.plain: The caller continues; results arrive later.
terminology.precise: Official Timing: nonblocking, queue, or message-based; results and faults return via other operations.
terminology.non_example: Composite POST that still waits for all subrequests in that HTTP call.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Queueable Apex: an implementation tool, not the pattern.

terminology.plain: A copy is rows you store; a projection is a window.
terminology.precise: External objects are a schema projection over the source. Stored custom objects are data integration copies that need keys and reconciliation.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Big objects / archive: still stored data.

terminology.plain: They call us and change our stored data.
terminology.precise: Official pattern: remote system CRUD on Platform data. Style is inbound data/process, not virtualization.
terminology.non_example: Salesforce Connect query out to ERP.

when_to_use: When you must choose request/response versus event-driven versus batch versus data-virtualization styles.
When a UI must block on a remote result (request/response) versus only notify other systems (event-driven).
When how much forces a batch copy instead of per-click callouts.
When stakeholders want live remote rows and you must refuse a second stored copy (data virtualization).
When mapping these four styles to official Integration Patterns names in an interview.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this styles lesson as a substitute for REST vs SOAP vs Bulk vs GraphQL selection (INT-002).
Do not treat event-driven as 'no error handling'—retries live in INT-008 and events in INT-007.
Do not call a scheduled Salesforce copy data virtualization.
Do not implement Connect adapters here (INT-009) or OAuth here (INT-004).
Do not run request/response callouts in production from this lesson.

decision_table.signal: User or transaction is blocked until the remote answer is written back.
decision_table.not: Fire-and-forget event with no wait, and not a nightly batch for this click.
decision_table.why: Official Request and Reply waits for completion and tracks state from the response.

decision_table.signal: Salesforce must notify others; the click must finish without remote completion.
decision_table.choose: Event-driven Fire and Forget (events detailed in INT-007).
decision_table.not: Chained synchronous callouts to every consumer in one save.
decision_table.why: Fire and Forget acknowledges and returns control without waiting for remote completion.

decision_table.signal: Hundreds of thousands of rows must stay aligned on a schedule.
decision_table.why: Official batch pattern refreshes copies in a batch manner.

decision_table.signal: Users need live remote rows and you will not store a Salesforce copy.
decision_table.not: An hourly custom-object copy labeled 'near real time'.
decision_table.why: Official virtualization avoids persisting data that then must be reconciled.

limitations: Does not configure events, Bulk jobs, or Connect.
security_notes: Virtualization still authenticates to the remote system (named credentials).
Inbound Remote Call-In is an API surface.
common_mistakes: Blocking the UI on a warehouse batch job.

check: Style may need to be event-driven or async status.
Volume may be batch, not request/response.
You stored a copy; reconciling is INT-010.
If virtualized, check live errors and filters, not a stale table.

interview_questions.question: Explain request/response, event-driven, batch, and data-virtualization styles.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Request/response waits. Event-driven acknowledges and continues. Batch refreshes copies on a schedule. Data virtualization reads live without a Salesforce copy.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map them to official names: Request and Reply, Fire and Forget, Batch Data Synchronization, Data Virtualization. I keep INT-002 APIs as vehicles. A copy on any cadence is not virtualization. If the caller must wait, I will not pretend an event is request/response.
interview_questions.example: Credit-score click vs Closed Won notify vs nightly items vs live bins.

interview_questions.question: When is request/response the wrong style?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the user must not wait, how much is huge, or the remote work is a long batch job. Then event-driven or batch.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Official Request and Reply waits for completion. If ERP credit check takes minutes, blocking Lightning save fights governors and UX. I split: show In Progress, event-driven completion, Remote Call-In write-back. I do not just raise timeouts.
interview_questions.example: Two-minute warehouse allocation during Opportunity save.

interview_questions.question: Design the four-story ACME lab using only the four styles.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Score: request/response. Notify: event-driven. Items: batch. Bins: data virtualization. I will not one-API all four.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write wait/copy/volume for each. I name official patterns in the decision record. Candidate vehicles: named-credential REST for score (INT-006), platform events (INT-007), Bulk 2.0 (INT-002), Connect (INT-009). Auth later (INT-004).
interview_questions.example: Four LAB_ stories in one architecture review.
follow_ups: What if bins must be reported offline?

interview_questions.question: Stakeholders want 'real-time inventory' and also Salesforce reports on last night's numbers.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That is two styles: live virtualization for the page, plus a batch copy if reports need a stored snapshot. I will not pretend one style does both without saying so.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Official virtualization does not persist a copy. Reports on stored objects need data integration and reconciliation (INT-010). I make the extra copy explicit, with keys and cadence, not a hidden five-minute sync labeled virtualization.
interview_questions.example: Account related list live; finance report on LAB_Inv_Snapshot__c.

interview_questions.question: Trigger callout times out on Data Loader updates.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: How much turned a request/response style into a batch problem. I stop per-row wait and move to event-driven or batch.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: INT-001 how much was ignored. I check bulk trigger context. I do not raise timeout as architecture. I may publish events per successful chunk or run Bulk the other direction.

interview_questions.question: External object page shows errors; someone wants a cache table 'to virtualize better.'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A cache table is a copy, which is batch/data integration, not virtualization. I diagnose Connect/auth/remote availability first (INT-009/INT-004).
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Architects page: external objects hold no data. If we add LAB_cache__c we accept reconciliation. That may be valid but must be named batch, not 'better virtualization.'
interview_questions.example: OData endpoint is down during a demo, so the related list errors instead of showing a cached copy.

interview_questions.question: How do event-driven and batch cooperate?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Events can notify; batch can backfill or reconcile. CDC can feed downstream stores. They are not the same style.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Fire and Forget handles the interesting moment. Batch Data Synchronization heals drift. INT-007 replay is for missed events inside the retention window; it is not a nightly item-master substitute by itself. I keep names separate in the design record.
interview_questions.example: CDC on Account plus nightly customer-master reconcile.

interview_questions.question: Teach the restaurant-pass analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Waiter waits, ticket spike, nightly inventory, supplier window. It breaks when the supplier window is dark (remote down) and when governors are not kitchen rules I can invent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map the four styles, then say APIs are cookware, Composite is still waiting at the pass, and a second fridge is a copy. Connect licenses are not spices to guess, and a live OData outage is not a pretty freeze-frame of the kitchen.
